citations.F1: `serialize_event` issues one `SELECT ... FROM users` per event, so limit=1000 is 1,000 round trips; fetch actors once with `WHERE id = ANY($1)`
citations.F2: Dedupe uses `in` against a Python list, which is O(n²) ... use a `set` for membership.
citations.F3: Blocking `requests.get` inside the async handler stops the whole worker's event loop for up to 2 s per uncached IP ... switch to an async client (`httpx.AsyncClient`, shared)
citations.F4: add `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY events_org_id_created_at_idx ON events (org_id, created_at DESC)`
citations.F5: `_request_timings` grows one float per request forever ... replace with `collections.deque(maxlen=...)` or a fixed-bucket histogram
citations.F6: `_geo_cache` is an unbounded dict keyed on client IP with no eviction — second leak; bound it with an LRU cap and a TTL.
citations.F7: Baseline first: `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` on the events SELECT with org 4127 / 30 d, and 5× `curl -w %{time_total}` against the route for acme and a <50-event org; re-run both after each change below.
citations.F9: Do not ship the on-call proposal. 16 workers × pool max 50 × 6 pods = up to 4,800 Postgres connections ... a 60 s Redis cache still leaves every miss blocking the event loop
